sections.heading: Reconciling the capability panel above with this register
sections.body:
`internal/api/capabilities.go` hand-maintains a twelve-entry feature list, rendered at the top of this page as **What is enabled, and how**. Six entries compute their state from a heartbeat; six are hardcoded. It is the most-read status surface in the product, so where it disagrees with this register, that is a defect in the list rather than a difference of opinion.

The three defects that belonged to the panel itself are closed: it is gated at the tenant role like every other route (SEC-08), and it reports a failed probe as a 503 naming what it could not observe instead of answering 200 with a schema of v0 and an empty fleet (OBS-09). Reading `goose_db_version` directly rather than `cfg.MigrationsTable` (OBS-10) remains.

rows: Agrees now. The gate this entry used to paper over — a spec validated only after a real device had been allocated to it — is applied at submission.
"The only automatic release path in the system"

**Still the wrong sentence.** `farm.lease_expire_max_runtime` is a second automatic path. It is a legitimate one — `max_runtime` is a deadline the user wrote down — and it now fences and rearms like the others, but the entry reads `unavailable` while that path is still ending leases. Name the reaper, not the category.
On the demo the simulator is a second writer with different rules. True in production, misleading here.

The predicate is right now. The actuator is built with a real `node.NewClient` rather than a nil `HostRunner`, so "a host agent is present, so tiers 3 and 4 can act" is true when the agent beats instead of being false whatever it does.
Right answer and, now, the right reason: no enroller is beating HERE because USB discovery needs Linux, not because no enroller can start.
Overstates. No directory enumeration, no mkdir, sizes truncated above 4 GiB — and push, install and pull have never completed on this deployment.
Half fixed. The bytes are fetchable over HTTP now, so the artifact path survives the split-role deployment. Nothing still tells you when disk is reclaimable or how much.
True. Unscoped, which the entry does not say: one shared poller fans out one shared snapshot to every tenant.
Agrees, and the fix string works. This entry used to say `not_built` about code that exists and name a variable with no consumer — an open port somebody believed they had closed.
Agrees, and is still the most honest entry in the list. It is still contradicted elsewhere in the product: the revoke response body says the connection is refused at a host proxy that does not exist.

Five things an operator would reasonably assume exist are still not in the list at all: host drain and selector placement (both now `met`, and invisible), the witness (`partial`, and the one that decides whether a control-plane outage costs a job its device), per-role metrics (`met`), and reset profiles (`not_built`). A feature list that names only built features cannot warn you about the ones you assumed — and, once they are built, cannot tell you they arrived.

sections.heading: Where the requirements came from
sections.body: Nine commits, six area pages and three external findings. The column worth reading is the last one: in five of the nine commits the notable thing is a defect found by **running** the code rather than by reading it, and in three of those the defect would have destroyed a healthy device or a healthy job.

rows: The founding commit. Fixes three blockers a design critique flagged; all three still hold.
Three defects found by running the SQL against PostgreSQL 17.10 rather than reading it, including a witness comparison no live lease could ever match.
Tiers stored rather than hard-coded; quarantine scoped so six devices on one hub is one incident.
The import-barrier test caught a comment this commit's own author wrote, which is the point of it.
A serial alone identifies nothing. The clone flag is only computable after the insert, because the second clone's own lookup still counts one.
Hardening caught `pm clear` failing on a package that is not installed — every first reset of every newly enrolled device would have quarantined a healthy phone for being clean.
Four defects found by running it: no file transfer at all, a decorative per-transfer context, pointer payloads skipping every validation rule, and `Kind()` panicking on a typed nil.
No default role, so a manifest with a typo fails instead of starting something plausible.
`TEST-06`, and the 88 gap entries behind most rows above
304 examples executed, 108 wrong, 98 claims corrected. The ratio is the argument for the method.
Four suppliers, four separate clauses. The finding that makes this a hardware project.
Novec 1230 at 8.5 vol% failed to suppress and failed to prevent propagation; propagation occurred in pure nitrogen.
IFC Table 1207.1.1: 20 kWh. ~60 handsets is about 1 kWh.

sections.heading: What the register argues for next
sections.body:
Ordered by unblocked-per-unit-of-work, not by severity. The previous ten are done — the witness loop, the reaper's kill switch, bulk exclusions, the charge-policy loop, both halves of the fence proxy, the per-job knobs, the alert rules and runbooks, tenant scope, and the tests — which is why this list looks different in kind. The cheap call sites for expensive, already-written machinery are exhausted. What is left is either work that has to be built, or work that cannot be finished at a desk.

The first item is not code, and it is first because six rows are waiting behind it.
bullets: **1. Run it against a rack.** `DEV-04`, `DEV-05`, `REC-03`, `OPS-04`, `HW-05` and `JOB-04` are all one sentence: this tree has never met a handset. Enrollment, topology discovery, `USBDEVFS_RESET`, `uhubctl` VBUS switching and the fence proxy's host half are written and covered against `fstest.MapFS` and `test/fakeadb`, and none of that is a phone. Nothing else in this list unblocks as much, and no amount of further code will substitute for it.

**2. `JOB-08` — show which step failed and what it printed.** `farm.job_steps` carries the state, the timing and the detail; no API route and no dashboard panel renders a step's output, so the answer to "why did this job fail" is a `psql` session. The rows exist; this is a read surface.

**3. `JOB-10` — make a job's reported state agree with its step rows.** A job can read `succeeded` beside a step still marked `running`. The abandoned-step case that produced it in the demo is fixed, but the reconciliation that would make the disagreement impossible is not written, and a status that can be wrong is worse than one that is missing.

**4. `LEASE-14` — make the ending recoverable from the event log at 3am.** `migrations/00007_lease_events.sql` writes an event on every transition; what is missing is the query, and the page, that turns those rows into "this lease ended at 02:14 because the job said so" without a join written by hand.

**5. `SEC-03` — record who, not only what.** `farm.audit_log` has an `actor` column and every operator route fills it, but the token that authenticated the actor is not distinguished from the name the token carries, so two humans sharing a token are one row.

**6. `API-07` — validate `ctl` against the server.** `ctl` validates a job spec locally against its own build of `internal/jobspec`. A client older than the control plane refuses a spec the server would accept; a newer one accepts what the server refuses. The server is the authority and `GET /api/v1/specs/kinds` already publishes the vocabulary.

**7. `API-06` — finish the exit-code contract.** `ExitCode` returns 4 for a partial bulk run now. What is still conflated is a control-plane failure with a target failure in the single-target commands, which is the difference between "retry" and "go look at that phone".

**8. `DEV-02` — make `resolve_device` rung 3 answer `ambiguous`.** It sets the verdict and leaves `v_dev` NULL, and rung 4 tests only `IF v_dev IS NULL`, so the verdict is computed and then not acted on.

**9. `DEV-07` — reconcile a hub that vanishes.** `topo.Config.RetireVanished` is reachable from configuration now (`FARM_TOPO_RETIRE_VANISHED`) and defaults off, so a port the kernel stops reporting stays an active, empty slot forever. Turning it on needs the bounded-retire path exercised against a real host, which is item 1 again.

**10. `OBS-10` — honour `FARM_MIGRATIONS_TABLE` everywhere.** One knob, read by the migrator and ignored by the code that reports the schema version, so a farm that renamed the table reports `0` on a fully migrated database.

sections.heading: Gaps closed since this register was written
sections.body:
Recorded rather than deleted, for the reason the six area pages give: a reader who remembers a gap has to be able to tell **fixed** from **never there**, and the change that closed one is usually the shortest true description of what the behaviour is now.

Eleven of the twenty-two entries below closed, and six more narrowed rather than vanished — which is the more interesting half. `LEASE-09` and `SEC-04` both went from "not built" to "built and not started", a state that is more specific and more embarrassing than absence: the expensive work is done and the call site is missing.

rows: `OPS-04`: `farmd node` cannot start in any environment. `runNode` passes `Addr: cfg.NodeAddr` and never passes `Token`, `node.New` errors whenever `Addr != "" && Token == ""`, and `FARM_NODE_ADDR` cannot be blanked because the config loader treats an empty value as unset and substitutes the `:8082` default.

`runNode` passes `Token: os.Getenv("FARM_NODE_TOKEN")` alongside `Addr`, so the guard that refused an unauthenticated USB-power endpoint is satisfiable. Run here with `FARM_HOST_ID` and the token set, the agent gets through configuration, heartbeats as `node, enroll`, and stops at USB discovery — which needs Linux. It predicted it would unblock four rows and it did: `DEV-04`, `DEV-05`, `REC-03`, `HW-06`.

`JOB-05`: the spec gate is written and never called. `specSubmissionError` is documented at `internal/api/specs.go:565` as "the gate POST /api/v1/jobs applies to a spec" and `grep -rn specSubmissionError` returns its comment and its definition, nothing else.
`internal/api/jobs_submit.go:215` calls it. Seven jobs had failed with `jobspec: invalid spec` after each burning an attempt on a different real device.

`SEC-02`: the remedy the product prints for its own open port does not work. `authInfo()` reports the fix as "set FARM_API_TOKENS to a token list"; `api.AuthenticatorFromEnv`, the only function that reads that variable, has zero callers anywhere in the tree.

`cmd/farmd/roles.go:321` calls `api.AuthenticatorFor(cfg, log)`, which reads `FARM_API_TOKENS` and REFUSES to start an exposed listener with no credentials rather than booting open. Verified live: 401 without a credential, 200 with one.

`REC-07`: host drain is written and never read. `POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/drain` sets `farm.hosts.admin_state='draining'` and returns "no new leases will be placed on this host". `farm.hosts` occurs once in `migrations/00002_lease.sql`, inside a GRANT, and both `admin_state` checks in `lease_acquire` are on the device, not the host.

`farm.lease_acquire` joins `farm.hosts` and requires `h.admin_state = 'enabled'` in both allocation queries (`migrations/00005_correctness.sql`). The allocator had been filtering the DEVICE's admin_state and never the host's.

`JOB-11`: `farm.jobs.selector` is stored, validated, echoed by the API and never used for placement. The string `selector` does not occur anywhere in `migrations/00002_lease.sql`, and `internal/lease/store.go` documents `ErrNoCapacity` as "no device … matched the job's selector", which is not what the SQL does.

`farm.device_matches` and `farm.selector_unknown_keys` land in `00005`, and `lease_acquire` filters on the first in both allocation queries. A selector key the schema does not support is now an exception naming the supported keys, rather than a filter that silently matched everything.

`OBS-03`: registering the role collectors is not a one-line fix, and attempting it as one breaks the binary. `internal/obs` declares namespace `farm` + name `recovery_attempts_total` with `{tier,outcome,host,hub,rack_slot}`; `internal/recovery` declares namespace `farm` + subsystem `recovery` + name `attempts_total` with `{tier,outcome}`. Both resolve to `farm_recovery_attempts_total`.

Sequenced exactly as this entry instructed: the colliding declaration was resolved first, then all ten `Collectors()` groups were registered. 92 distinct `farm_*` names on a live `/metrics`, against 15.

`DEV-02` and `HW-07`: `farm.resolve_device` rung 2 calls `min()` on a `uuid` column and PostgreSQL 17 has no `min(uuid)` aggregate, while `docker-compose.yml` pins `postgres:17-alpine` and nothing anywhere declares a version requirement.

Rung 2 was rewritten to count and fetch separately, so the `min(uuid)` that raised 42883 on the second-strongest identity signal — in exactly the duplicate-fingerprint case it exists to adjudicate — is gone (`00005`). Rung 3 now reports `ambiguous` instead of being overwritten by the adoption branch (`00011`).

`OPS-07`: no Helm chart and no Kubernetes manifests. `docker-compose.yml` is the only deployment artifact in the repository, while the README's architecture diagram places the whole control plane in Kubernetes.

`deploy/helm/device-farmer` ships one Deployment per role, and fails the render if `config.extra` carries `DATABASE_URL`, `FARM_API_TOKENS` or `FARM_COMPONENT` — the last because one shared component name makes the reaper's gap accounting blind to the role that is down, so its outage goes unrefunded and its leases are reclaimed on schedule.

`OBS-09`: the capability panel at the top of this page cannot tell "I measured zero" from "I could not measure". `schemaInfo` and `fleetCounts` discard their query error with `_ =`, `roleStatuses` populates its map only `if err == nil`, and `handleCapabilities` returns 200 in every case.

Each probe returns its error and a report that could not be taken is a 503 naming which observation is missing and what must not be concluded from it: the schema is unknown and it is NOT v0; the counts are unknown and they are NOT zero. An empty `goose_db_version` is kept as an ANSWER, because a fresh database that genuinely needs migrating is the case the note was written for.

`SEC-08`: `GET /api/v1/capabilities` is the one route in `buildHandler` registered with a bare `mux.HandleFunc` rather than through `tenant(...)` or `operator(...)`, so it carries no role — which is also why `API-02`, the invariant that no endpoint can exist without a level, reads `partial` rather than `met`.

Registered through `tenant(...)` like every other route. Tenant is the lowest role there is, which is the design: under an open authenticator the stub grants every caller operator, so the debugging case the route was left open for still reaches it, and the same line starts asking for a credential the moment `FARM_API_TOKENS` is set.

The capability panel at the top of this page disagrees with the register in three places: `Automatic reclamation` claims to be the only automatic release path (`LEASE-08` says otherwise), `Recovery ladder` branches its detail on whether a `node` role is beating when the deciding fact is that `HostRunner` is nil at `cmd/farmd/roles.go:206`, and `Authentication` prints a fix that does nothing.

All three are gone. The reclamation entry is still worth rewording — `max_runtime` is a second automatic ending — but the recovery-ladder predicate is now correct (the actuator holds a real `node.Client`), authentication reports `unavailable` with a fix string that works, and the Helm entry reports `enabled`.

`SEC-04`: the fence is still not enforced at the resource, and the product's own revoke response still says it is. What changed is that the design and a testable skeleton now exist — `docs/design/fence-proxy.md` and `internal/fenceproxy`, 24 tests — and nothing constructs either, so no ADB byte passes through a proxy today. The package is deliberately inert and structurally barred from ever ending a lease: two tests enforce that, one asserting `FenceSource` has exactly one method because a second is what would let a refusal DO something.

Both halves ship, off unless the certificates are configured: `internal/fenceproxy` behind an mTLS listener the node agent serves, and `adbwire.WithAdmissionPreamble` + `WithTLS` on every client connection. The revoke response and the capability row now describe THIS PROCESS's side of the wire, because enforcement is per host and no single process can see which hosts run a proxy.

`JOB-06`: reset tiers expand to nothing. `farm.jobs.profile_id` is never written by any code path — two hits in the tree, both reads — and the reset expansion needs a profile to know which packages a job did not install.

`internal/api/jobs_submit.go` writes `profile_id`, `reset_tier`, `max_attempts` and `resumable` from the submission. This entry was written against a tree that already had them — a register revised only downward is not being checked.

`LEASE-09`: nothing STARTS a witness. Every part exists now — `farm.lease_witness`, `Store.Witness`, `Holder.StartWitness`, the on-device marker in `internal/runner/witness.go`, and both config knobs — and every `StartWitness` call site in the tree is a test. `config.Summary()` reports `NOT STARTED` rather than printing the interval as if in force. The last unwired half of the #663 countermeasure, and the top of this page's next-steps list.

The jobrunner starts a marker and a witness loop per placement. Watched doing it on 2026-09-05: `farm.leases.witness_at` set thirty seconds into a hundred-second step, `witness_extensions=1`, `reclaimable_at` pushed forty-five minutes out, `farm_jobrunner_witness_total{outcome="accepted"} 1`.

`DEV-09`: the watchdog now reads battery level and temperature on its own ticker and writes `battery_pct` and `battery_temp_dc`, which had no producer outside the demo seed since 00001; `00010` adds the CHECK the temperature column never had. Exercised against the fake ADB server, never against a handset. `charge_gate` still has no writer: the agent-side verb exists (`internal/node/chargegate.go`, a held set-point with a dead-man's switch that fails safe to ON) and the policy loop that would drive it does not.

`migrations/00016_battery_readings.sql` keeps the series, `internal/watchdog/swell.go` raises `battery_anomaly` on a temperature rise, an absolute ceiling or an idle-drain rate, and `internal/chargepolicy` holds idle devices inside a 40–80% band through the host agent's charge gate. No lease is touched by any of it.

`TEST-04` and `TEST-05`: the two loops that decide allocation and release, and the two that execute work on a device, now have 7,466 lines of tests between them — including the fenced-release branch, which needed a seam because it can otherwise only be exercised against a live Postgres and a running renewal loop. `isRetryable` and `planResume` are still untested, and a regression in either reintroduces #663.

The decision points are covered and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the whole recipe on every change: build, vet, gofmt, the Go suite, a migration from empty against Postgres 17, every `test/assertions*.sql`, and `helm lint`.

`LEASE-08`: `farm.lease_expire_max_runtime` fences and rearms like every other ending now (`00005`), so the hole this entry was written about is closed. What remains is narrower and is really `LEASE-11`: it is a second automatic ending that the reaper's kill switch and quiesce gate do not reach. Whether they SHOULD is a design question nobody has answered in writing — `max_runtime` is a deadline the user wrote down, which the founding requirement names as a legitimate ending.
Closed by `00005` as this entry already recorded; kept here so a reader who remembers the gap can tell fixed from never-there.

`LEASE-03`: the Postgres role firewall is correct DDL that no deployment assumes. `farm_reaper`, `farm_scheduler` and `farm_watchdog` are created `NOLOGIN` with the right grants; no Go code issues `SET ROLE`, there is no per-component DSN, and every process connects with one `DATABASE_URL` — as `farm`, which on the demo is a superuser.

`FARM_DB_ROLE` assumes the role — `SET ROLE` in the pool's `AfterConnect`, refused at startup when the login user is not a member — and `migrations/00015_runtime_roles.sql` completes the grants each loop needs. `test/assertions_v15.sql` runs each loop's whole pass as its own role: the reaper cannot read `farm.device_runtime`, the watchdog cannot read `farm.leases`, and that pass ends no lease.

gaps.what: `HW-03`: clean-agent suppression does not stop a lithium event — Novec 1230 at 8.5 vol% failed both to suppress and to prevent propagation, which occurred even in pure nitrogen — so the mitigations that work are physical and procedural: containment, spacing, charge limiting, early detection. Two of the four now have product support: `docs/siting.md` covers containment and spacing, and the battery reader supplies the early-detection signal. Charge limiting has both halves it needed — the agent-side gate and the parked state that stops a deliberately dark device being quarantined as a fault — and no loop between them.
gaps.consequence: The mitigations that work are containment, cell-to-cell spacing, charge limiting and early detection. The first two are rack design and are outside the software. The second two are `DEV-09`, which is unwritten. The failure mode this entry exists to prevent is buying a clean-agent bottle and considering the hazard handled — the measured result says it will neither put the fire out nor stop it spreading. Note also that fire code is not the gate here: `HW-04`. What the product can do, it now does: `internal/chargepolicy` parks idle devices above 80% and releases them below 40%, `internal/watchdog/swell.go` raises `battery_anomaly` on a temperature rise or an idle-drain rate, and `DeviceFarmerBatteryAnomaly` pages carrying `rack_slot`, because a human walks to a position. None of that is suppression.

gaps.what: `DEV-05`: topology discovery and enrollment run only inside the `farmd node` role, and `topo.Sysfs` refuses on any GOOS but Linux. Nothing in this repository can enroll a device or register a slot on a Windows or macOS host.
gaps.consequence: The Linux restriction is correct and unavoidable — `/sys/bus/usb/devices`, `USBDEVFS_RESET` and per-port VBUS have no equivalent elsewhere. What is worth knowing is that on Linux it is still unreachable, because of `OPS-04`. So `farm.identity_observations` and `farm.slot_occupancy` are empty on every deployment, all 56 devices carry `hw_fingerprint IS NULL`, and everything documented about the identity ladder was verified by calling its SQL and its Go functions directly rather than by watching the loop run.

gaps.what: `JOB-04`: checkpoint and resume are implemented and have never executed. The demo has never exercised the resume path, `internal/runner` has no test files, and `runner.Conn` is documented as an interface specifically so `planResume` and `isRetryable` could be driven by a fake without a phone — the fake does not exist.
gaps.consequence: Resume is the feature that makes a six-hour job survive a pod eviction, which is one of the two reasons the lease protocol was built the way it was. Its correctness currently rests on reading the code. Treat a resume in production as a first run: watch it, and expect the idempotent flag on `farm.step_kinds` to be the thing that decides whether a re-run repeats a side effect.

gaps.what: This register is a point-in-time verification and nothing re-checks it — and the cost of that is now measured rather than predicted. It was written on `ca91c1c`; by the time it was next read, 36 of its 101 rows were wrong, because migration `00005` and nine merged branches had landed underneath it. Every status is still confirmed by a command a reader can re-run, and nothing runs them on a schedule. A register that decays silently is a gap list that will one day be read as reassurance.
gaps.consequence: A row that reads `not_built` after somebody has built the thing is the same failure this page exists to prevent, pointed the other way. The cheapest guard is to treat the greps in the examples above as the register's test suite: each is a single command whose output is printed beside it, so a status is falsifiable in one paste. Until `TEST-05` exists there is nothing to hang them on.
